items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Narrator
Your no-cost EMI can cost about twenty percent more than paying cash. How is that free?
Narrator
The deal: a three hundred dollar phone, six easy payments, zero interest.
Narrator
But the bank still charges interest. The store just hides it.
Chars
[smug, deep, rich gold bar, very pleased with himself] Free money? Even I'm not that shiny.
Narrator
So where does the interest go?
Narrator
Into the discount. Say cash buyers pay two hundred and fifty-five dollars. You skip that discount and pay three hundred.
Narrator
Then tax on that hidden interest, plus a processing fee.
Narrator
And here's the part almost nobody reads.
Narrator
In twenty thirteen, India's central bank said zero percent interest doesn't exist.
Narrator
That's the mirage: the interest didn't vanish. It moved into the price.
Narrator
In this example, you pay about twenty-one percent more, for the same phone.
Chars
[delighted, squeaky banknote, surprised to be winning] Wait. Cash is the discount?
Narrator
So no cost does mean no cost... for the store.
Narrator
Comment: do you check the cash price first?
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
